newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool j/v deal being negotiated-WI.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool j/v deal being negotiated-WI.

text.p: Wool International (WI), Elders Australia Ltd and Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd are still negotiating major matters such as capital structure for the planned forward sales joint venture for wool, WI director Charles Armstrong told the New South Wales Farmers' Association. Other points under negotiation include contributions to the joint-venture, what assets would be included, the value of assets, board composition and other issues, he said.
"Obviously there's nothing concrete that (can be said yet) about most of the intricate detail," he said.
The joint-venture was still basically a concept, he said.
"But it's a concept agreed to by those three parties that it does provide some real benefits for the total industry," Armstrong said.
The original Wool International Holdings (WIH) proposal for forward marketing and risk management was still top priority within the concept of the joint-venture, he said.
None of the WIH proposals had changed.
But the concept had been broadened significantly with the new proposal, he said.
One of the real advantages for WI of merging with the two brokers was that they were commercial, profit-drioven partners.
Some of those who would have been customers of WIH viewed that as a very positive move, Armstrong said.
It was proposed that the joint-venture would take over all activities associated with selling wool after receival into store, he said.
Armstrong's comments follow an October 1 announcement by participants in the proposed joint-venture announcing the plan.
The proposal is aimed at developing a forward market for Australian wool to enhance its competitiveness.
An estimated 85 to 95 percent of Australian wool is currently sold on a spot basis.
Elders and Wesfarmers Dalgety account for about 60 percent of the auction-based movement of wool in Australia.
Wool International is currently responsible for selling the Australian wool stockpile. WIH is the vehicle for WI's drive to introduce a forward-sales strategy for Australian wool.
